summary: The proofs of (1), (2), the exact family, and its limit (5) are mathematically sound. However, the candidate statement also asserts that no bound with A >= 1/2 is refuted by this family. That assertion is false for specified positive coefficients, so the complete candidate cannot be approved as stated.
critical_errors: The assertion 'No bound with A >= 1/2 is refuted by this family' is false. Take A = 1/2 and c = 2. Equation (5) gives sqrt(M(1 + log M)) times the right mean half-line probability tending to sqrt(2), which is strictly less than 2. Consequently, for all sufficiently large T this same family violates the lower bound 2/[sqrt(M)(1 + log M)^(1/2)]. Thus the family does refute a bound with A = 1/2, even eventually. A limit of sqrt(2) only leaves open the existence of a bound with a suitable smaller coefficient; it cannot justify the universal assertion about all bounds at this exponent.
repair_hints: Distinguish refuting every positive coefficient at an exponent from refuting individual coefficients. The established asymptotics do not exclude the existence of a suitable positive coefficient for A >= 1/2, but they do refute coefficients greater than sqrt(2) at A = 1/2.
